item.title: Is a Two-Sample t-Test Appropriate? Delivery Times for Two Couriers
item.stimulus: A dispatcher wants to know whether two couriers have different mean delivery times. Each courier has made thousands of deliveries. The dispatcher independently and randomly selected 34 deliveries by the first courier (sample mean 41.6 minutes) and 12 deliveries by the second courier (sample mean 44.9 minutes). A dotplot of the 34 first-courier times has no strong skewness and no outliers. A dotplot of the 12 second-courier times is skewed right with one outlier.

parts.prompt: Let μ₁ be the mean for the first courier and μ₂ the mean for the second courier. Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean delivery time, in minutes, of all deliveries by the first courier, and μ₂ is the true mean delivery time of all deliveries by the second courier.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean delivery time, in minutes, of all deliveries by the first courier, and μ₂ is the true mean delivery time of all deliveries by the second courier, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ ≠ 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ ≠ 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure, and decide whether its conditions are met. Justify each decision.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the deliveries were selected by independent random samples from the two couriers' deliveries.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the deliveries were selected by independent random samples from the two couriers' deliveries.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of deliveries by its courier.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of deliveries by its courier.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: one sample (n = 12) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the second courier's sample is skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition, says whether it is met, and gives the reason: one sample (n = 12) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the second courier's sample is skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean delivery time, in minutes, of all deliveries by the first courier, and μ₂ is the true mean delivery time of all deliveries by the second courier. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ ≠ 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means. Randomization: the deliveries were selected by independent random samples from the two couriers' deliveries. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of deliveries by its courier. Sample-data condition: one sample (n = 12) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the second courier's sample is skewed with one outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
item.verification_python:
n1, n2 = 34, 12
both_big = min(n1, n2) >= 30
assert both_big == False
assert 41.6 != 44.9
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
